Matching Headings

Exercise 1: The History of Everyday Things

Match the headings A–G with paragraphs 1–5. There are two extra headings. Use each heading only once.

  1. An accident that changed the way we cook
  2. A failed experiment that became useful
  3. A misunderstanding that created a new habit
  4. A solution to a factory problem
  5. From work equipment to everyday entertainment
  6. An invention that was too expensive to become popular
  7. A product designed especially for travellers

1.

The microwave oven was invented by accident. In 1945, an engineer named Percy Spencer was working with radar equipment when he noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted. He became curious and tried the same experiment with popcorn and an egg. Soon, he realized that microwaves could heat food very quickly. The first microwave ovens were huge and expensive, but today they are found in kitchens all over the world.

2.

Post-it Notes also appeared because of a mistake. A scientist was trying to create a very strong glue, but instead he made one that was weak and could be removed easily. At first, nobody knew what to do with it. Years later, another employee used the glue to keep small pieces of paper inside his book. The idea worked perfectly, and the famous yellow notes were born.

3.

The tea bag was not originally designed to be put into hot water. In the early 1900s, a tea seller sent small samples of tea to customers in silk bags. Some customers thought they were supposed to put the whole bag into the teapot. The method was simple and convenient, so tea bags quickly became popular. Later, paper bags replaced the more expensive silk ones.

4.

The QR code was created in Japan in the 1990s. A car company needed a faster way to track parts in its factories. Ordinary barcodes could not store enough information, so engineers designed a new square code that could be scanned from different directions. Today, QR codes are used for menus, payments, tickets, websites, and many other everyday tasks.

5.

The first modern headphones were developed for communication, not music. Early versions were used by telephone operators and radio workers. Over time, the technology became smaller, lighter, and more comfortable. In the 20th century, headphones became popular with music lovers, and later with gamers and people using smartphones. Today, many people wear them every day without thinking about their original purpose.
